scope: Independent all-shared-time saved full-density reconstruction, whole-native-quadrature moment comparison, observed temporal order, frozen plot series, provenance, analytic controls, and media audit. Density L1 reconstruction is restricted to the documented cubes [-4,4]^3 and [-5,5]^3; no full-domain density convergence claim.

three_grid_and_time_levels.reason: Three-level claims need both the coarse and fine trajectories completed; coarse accuracy need not meet the finest 1% target.

quadrature_figure_arrays.scope: Reference_curve displays exp(-z²/2) functionvalues; q are integrationweights. Physical axisweights independently reconstruct the fixed volume quadrature.

independent_convergence_plot.scope: Values below the display lower bound use left triangles only for rendering; saved error values and acceptance criteria remain exact. Frozen plot block replayed without evolution solver.

four_operator_independent_arrays.scope: Frozen plot fragment only, no solver. Plotted Landau moments independently recomputed from all native saved densitynodes; Lorentz Legendre and OU formulas independently derived for same physicalGaussian.
four_operator_independent_arrays.terminal_table_scope: Same physical initial Gaussian and independently matched initial pressure slope. Landau values use whole native saved density; Lorentz fourth moments follow exact P2/P4 angular decay and conserve speed-fourth moment; Dougherty is the exact OU solution; constrained local initial log density lies in its nullspace. This is a moment comparison, not a full-density equivalence claim.

observed_cost_scope: Recorded shared-machine costs paired with disagreement relative to measured baseline densityincrements, not a continuum finite-time error oracle; casewall includes startup/oracle/compilation, acceptedstep wall includes compiledsolve work; processpeakRSS is aggregate, not percase. No isolated speedup or equal-error speed ranking is inferred.

empirical_temporal_order.scope: Empirical finite-interval difference ratio and log2 ratio. This is not a temporal-order theorem or continuum error estimate.
